texts.facts: The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent manner of driver of Cement Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03- TK-3605 and the Yelahanka Traffic police have registered the case against the driver of said Lorry in Cr.No.60/2022 for the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC. The 1st respondent being the R.C. owner and the 2 nd respondent being the insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Chandradev Singh vs Haridoss.V on 16 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143627002/ 2 4.
texts.arguments: The petitioner drove his vehicle during wee hours. As such, on Chandradev Singh vs Haridoss.V on 16 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143627002/ 4 account of negligence the petitioner dashed behind the lorry. Therefore, there is no negligence on the part of driver of insured lorry. In the line of the arguments canvassed by the 2 nd respondent counsel, she relied on the decision of Hon'ble Apex court decided in Civil Appeal No.10145 of 2016, between Nishan Singh and Others Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., and Others. Due to negligent parking of insured lorry, the accident took place. There was no negligence on the part of petitioner. Moreover, the investigation officer thoroughly investigated the case and filed the chare sheet against the driver of offending vehicle/insured lorry. As such, there is no contributory negligence from the side of petitioner.

The petitioner has produced discharge summaries and same have been marked as Ex.P.10.

He has averred that, he was a delivery boy at Dunzo and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But he has not produced documents to substantiate the same.
Hence, this Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Hence, two months is to be considered as loss of income during laidup period.
